audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Aurora Level 1 and Jax Levels 2, 3 and 4-5 — the reverse of what the page's own whys say. whys[0] ends "the edge is faintly his"; whys[1] says he "can only walk up into chip damage with no answer yet"; whys[3] says "your Q-recast burst plus passive sustain out-trades him in this window".
audit.why: The packet chart already reads Jax / Aurora / Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Jax / Jax, matching every one of those sentences.
audit.corrected: Jax / Aurora / Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Jax / Jax with ratings matched. diff stays TRICKY 7.5/10 at 46.34%.

audit.whatIsWrong: His ultimate is called "Grandmaster's Might" in three places, and Aurora's is called "Between the Worlds". No cooldowns anywhere.
audit.why: Jax's ultimate is Grandmaster-at-Arms (110/100/90s) — "Grandmaster's Might" is the retired name. Aurora's is Between Worlds (140/120/100s). Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s, Leap Strike 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s at 700 range, Empower 7/6/5/4/3s. Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 and only 9s at rank 5 — the punish window shrinks by nearly half over the lane, which is the real reason the matchup decays.
audit.corrected: Real names and cooldowns throughout, with the rank-1-to-rank-5 shrink stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says four times that Counter Strike dodges your Q's second hit — wants.foe[1] is explicit: "Hold Counter Strike to dodge your Q's second hit and autos".
audit.why: Riot's text for Counter Strike: Jax "dodges all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattacks". It dodges attacks, not abilities. Twofold Hex, its recast pull, The Weirding and Between Worlds all land on a Jax sitting in Counter Strike — only your basic attacks are dodged. An Aurora who holds her whole combo for a spell that cannot stop it hands him the trade for free. Two more additions: Grandmaster-at-Arms grants Armor and Magic Resist on activation, so bursting into an active R is the worst possible timing; and Empower is his auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell rather than the cast.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike stated as an attack-dodge only; the MR gain on Grandmaster-at-Arms and the Empower auto-reset added.

audit.why: Counter Strike goes 17s to 9s across its ranks, which changes the whole shape of the lane.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike 17s to 9s, Leap Strike 8s at 700, Empower 7s, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110s.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.whys[2] sits in the Level 3 slot but opens "Levels 4-5 cancel out"; the "KA answer / a immobile drain bot" line appears four times; the Between Worlds untargetability claim appears in four places.

notes: Biggest error: the page repeatedly says Counter Strike dodges Aurora's Q second hit. Riot's text is "dodge all incoming attacks" — attacks, not abilities. Twofold Hex, its recast pull, The Weirding and Between Worlds all land on a Jax standing in Counter Strike; only her autos are dodged. That reversal makes an Aurora hold her entire combo for no reason. Also: his ultimate is Grandmaster-at-Arms, not "Grandmaster's Might" (retired name, used in three places), and it grants Armor and Magic Resist on activation, so bursting into it is the worst timing available — the page never said so. The suspectNames entries for "Leap Strikes", "Counter Strikes" and "Counter Strike's" are FALSE POSITIVES: those are correct verb and possessive forms of the real names, and I left them alone. BAD DERIVED FLAG: the kit file tags Empower (W) as a "dash"; Riot's description is only "charges his weapon with energy, causing his next attack to deal additional damage" — no movement. I wrote no dash interaction for his W.
